name: lpqi_spad64_i2cass
label: LPQI-Pathfinder IMSE 64x64 SPAD array (I2CASS, LiDAR heritage)
sources: Quintana, Gonzalez-de-Rivera, Lopez-Buedo & Prada 2026, Sensors 26, 5757 (doi:10.3390/s26185757): the LPQI-Pathfinder 64 x 64 I2CASS/IMSE SPAD array and its AER readout
Cosentino et al. 2026, SPIE AS 14149AN: Peltier-cooled camera head at -20 C, FPGA acquisition
Prada et al. 2024 (arXiv:2406.14704): the same array on a 10-inch telescope (Betelgeuse occultation, SDSS g)
notes: Effective PDE 0.026 = fill factor 0.035 x peak PDP 0.75 (Sensors paper, Table 1 and Sec. 2); the wavelength dependence is not published, so the value is taken flat over 400-900 nm.

Timing: the array has no per-event time stamps yet (AER events only); the paper's roadmap targets ~500 ps end-to-end with White Rabbit time stamping (10-20 ps synchronization jitter, 81-96 ps demonstrated on a previous Zynq) -- 500 ps FWHM is that target, not a measurement.
Dead time 5-10 ns (paper: 'typical dead times of 5-10 ns'); dark count rate median 1.68 Hz per pixel at 27.8 C (lower when cooled to -20 C).
max_total_cps 6.7e6 is the implemented AER-to-AXI capture ceiling (100 MHz / 15 cycles per event); the chip's own AER arbitration ceiling is 4e7 events/s.

n_pixels 25: a ~1 arcsec seeing disk over the 0.18 arcsec (NOT) / 0.13 arcsec (TNG) pixels of a 24.5 um pitch at the natural focus (plate scales from the paper), i.e. the dead time and dark counts of ~5 x 5 pixels per telescope.
Sky at ORM (21.70 mag/arcsec^2 V): ~3 incident photons/s/pixel (paper Eq. 1), negligible against the stellar rates here.
